To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CARS signal is proportional to the square of the molecular hyper-polarizability and is proportional to the fourth power of the molecular concentration.
the coherent active spectroscopy (C.R.S.) of randomly oriented molecules is possible and that the C.A.R.S. signal intensity is maximum for finely dispersed samples.
the CARS signal is proportional to the square of the hyperpolarizablity of the molecule and that the signal is proportional to a product of the number of molecules and their hyperpolarizabilty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical and experimental investigation of the coherent Raman (anti-stokes) spectroscopy of randomly oriented molecules and crystals in the form of a fine powder.

a new method of active spectroscopy, coherent active Raman spectroscopy (CARE), which has the following advantages: (1) the signal intensity is independent of the concentration of the medium, (2) a wide range of frequencies can be covered, (3) the spectral resolution is not limited by the width of the exciting radiation, and (4) the signal is not affected by the absorption of exciting radiation.
the development of the theory of coherent active spectroscopy of isotropic media formed from randomly oriented elements (liquids and crystalline powders).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ARS signal from finely dispersed samples is not a new effect.
the ARS method is a promising technique for obtaining new information about molecular systems.
the coherent Raman scattering of the third order is a very powerful tool for studying molecular systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have obtained the general theory for CARS of optically isotro-pic media formed by randomly orient-ed molecules and have demonstrated the possibility of using the method of coherent active spectroscopy for the investigation of molecular systems in the condensed state.
a new technique for the study of molecular structure and dynamics in optically isotropic systems has been developed.
the technique of irreducible tensors makes it possible to obtain the correct expression for the susceptibility tensor of a medium formed by randomly orientated molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ARS signal from an isotropic medium can be observed only in the presence of the quadratic nonlinear response of the medium.
the ARS signal can be used for coherent active spectroscopy of randomly oriented media.
CARS spectroscopy can be applied to study the optical properties of finely dispersed optically isotropic samples.
